writable_hooks.description: Allow the container to write to .git/hooks (default: false — hooks are mounted read-only)

name.description: Explicit commit author name installed in the container's global git config; takes precedence over the host's global git config. Trusted-scope only (ignored from project config).

email.description: Explicit commit author email installed in the container's global git config; takes precedence over the host's global git config. Trusted-scope only (ignored from project config).

seed_host_identity.description: Read the host's global git user.name/user.email and install it in the container when no explicit name/email is set (default: true). Set false to keep only the fail-closed guard. Trusted-scope only.

readonly.description: Lock the configured commit identity so the container agent cannot overwrite it: instead of writing ~/.gitconfig (which is writable), Coi mounts the identity read-only at ~/.gitconfig. This locks the WHOLE global gitconfig, so ANY `git config --global …` in the container fails read-only (use per-repo --local config for other settings). Only takes effect with a resolvable identity (name/email, or a seeded host identity); if it cannot be applied the session fails closed rather than falling back to writable. Trusted-scope only. Default false.

strip_attribution.description: Install a global commit-msg hook (core.hooksPath → /etc/coi/git-hooks, root-owned) that strips auto-injected AI attribution — `Co-Authored-By: <tool bot>` trailers and `Generated with …` footers — from every commit message, so commits carry only the configured author identity. Strip-don't-reject: never blocks a commit. For Claude Code it additionally enforces includeCoAuthoredBy=false via managed settings. Known limitations: a repo whose LOCAL git config sets core.hooksPath (e.g. husky) overrides the global hook, and `git commit --no-verify` skips commit-msg hooks. Default: true. Trusted-scope only.

strip_attribution_patterns.description: Replace the default strip patterns (grep -E extended regexes, matched per commit-message line) when non-empty. Trusted-scope only.

protected_branches.description: Branches the agent can't commit on or push to: root-owned git hooks refuse commits on them, moving them to a commit the remote doesn't already have (cherry-pick, merge, rebase, reset, ...), and pushes to them — so the agent works on a feature branch and opens a PR. Unset: ["main", "master"]. [] disables the guard. A list replaces the default. Trusted scope only: ignored (with a warning) from a project config or project profile, where the default stays on.
